definition: FullGround F is an arbitrary relation between a predicate-valued set of facts and an explanandum. Admission is primitive and does not entail actual truth, membership dependency, modal sufficiency or adequate explanation. It permits plural, infinite or empty sets; every admitted candidate set is quantified over in the terminus conclusion, not just one chosen set.
note: Analyst framework for #545, not independently established metaphysical applicability. See docs/notes/grounding-baseline-545.md for examples, exclusions, structural properties and strongest rival replies.
